items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had many friends who were going to the High School of Music and Art who would had graduated two years before me, who were in the band: Harry Hall, Larry Morton, Astley Fernell

ctx.x: Yeah—well I was 15, I guess. I had been very, very interested in Miles, of course, that was my idol. [I was] listening to his records as well as Clifford Brown. I have to say that I became kind of friendly with Miles, from that point. He used to go to a gym up on 137th Street and Broadway and I was always going to that train stop in hopes that I would see Miles Davis sometime, you know? (Laughs) I had stared to study with Donald Byrd who lived in the Bronx at that time. I was going to Donald Byrd because I had…

study with Donald Byrd. But, he was teaching me to be a better trumpet player, so he broke down my sound, and my tonguing, and knowledge of me knowing scales, and chords, and all of that stuff. After a number of months, he made me transcribe some solos. As a matter of fact, he gave me an assignment, the first assignment. I was taking lessons every week for $5. He said, “Okay, next week I want you to have a Kenny Dorham solo, and a Miles Davis solo transcribed.” Whew. (Laughs) Well, I learned the solos, but, to…
Could you go back and talk about Donald Byrd?
